aclfile: Path to ACL file (empty = no ACL file, use inline SETUSER rules only)
backup-sealed-ttl: Seconds a sealed backup is kept before it is cleaned up automatically; `0` keeps it until `BACKUP CLEANUP` (Redis 8.10 `backup-sealed-ttl`).
backupdirname: Directory `BACKUP START` writes a backup into, under the working directory (Redis 8.10 `backupdirname`). Startup-only.
cluster-announce-bus-port: Bus port announced to the cluster. 0 = `port` + 10000.
cluster-announce-hostname: Hostname this node announces to the cluster (Redis `cluster-announce-hostname`): letters, digits, `-` and `.`. Shown in CLUSTER NODES, SLOTS and SHARDS, and given to clients in place of the address when `cluster-preferred-endpoint-type` is `hostname`.
cluster-announce-ip: Address this node tells the rest of the cluster to reach it on (Redis `cluster-announce-ip`). Empty = let peers use the address they observe.
cluster-announce-port: Client port announced to the cluster. 0 = `port`.
cluster-bus-port-protected-mode: Refuse to run as a cluster node while the bus port is unauthenticated (Redis `cluster-bus-port-protected-mode`): with this `yes`, a cluster node needs `cluster-bus-secret`. The default `no` starts without one and logs a warning.
cluster-bus-secret: A secret every node of the cluster shares. A node connecting to another's bus port must prove it knows it (a challenge and an HMAC-SHA256 answer; the secret itself is never sent) before anything it says is read. Empty: the bus is open to anything that can reach it. Set it on every node or none.
cluster-enabled: True iff the server should run as a cluster node. Activated by `--cluster-enabled yes`. Defaults to false (standalone).
cluster-node-timeout: Milliseconds without a PONG before a peer is marked PFAIL. Default 15000 matches Redis. Lower values detect failures faster but increase false positives under network jitter.
cluster-preferred-endpoint-type: What clients are told to connect to, in MOVED, ASK and the topology replies: `ip`, `hostname` or `unknown-endpoint` (Redis `cluster-preferred-endpoint-type`).
cluster-require-full-coverage: Stop serving keyed commands while any hash slot is unassigned or owned by a failed node (Redis `cluster-require-full-coverage`).
dir: Working directory: where `dump.kdb`, `appendonly.aof`, backups and `nodes.conf` live (Redis `dir`). Empty = the directory the server was started in.
lfu-decay-time: Minutes for a key's use count to fall by one, for the LFU policies (Redis `lfu-decay-time`). 0 = it never falls.
lfu-log-factor: How slowly a key's use count grows, for the LFU policies (Redis `lfu-log-factor`).
log-format: Log line format: `text`, or `json` — one object per line, for log pipelines.
logfile: Write the log to this file, appending, instead of standard error.
loglevel: Log level: debug, verbose, notice (or info), warning, nothing. docs/LOGGING.md says what each shows.
lua-parallel-scripts: Run scripts whose KEYS share a hash tag beside each other, each under its tag's lock, instead of one at a time for the whole server. A script run that way may not touch a key outside the tag. On unless switched off; it means something only in a build with Lua. See docs/SCRIPTS.md.
masterauth: Password this node presents when connecting to its master as a replica (Redis `masterauth`). Required when the master has `requirepass` or ACLs; without it the handshake is refused.
masteruser: ACL user to authenticate as on the master (Redis `masteruser`). Empty = the `default` user.
maxmemory: Max memory (0 = unlimited): bytes, or with a unit as in Redis (`3gb`, `512mb`). Once the process uses more, writes are refused with an OOM error.
maxmemory-policy: What to do when `maxmemory` is reached (Redis `maxmemory-policy`): noeviction — refuse the write allkeys-lru | allkeys-lfu | allkeys-lrm | allkeys-random — delete keys to make room: the least recently used, least frequently used, least recently modified, or any volatile-lru | volatile-lfu | volatile-lrm | volatile-random | volatile-ttl — the same, among keys with a TTL only; or the one nearest to expiring
maxmemory-samples: How many keys are looked at to choose the one to evict (Redis `maxmemory-samples`).
min-replicas-max-lag: How recently, in seconds, a replica must have acknowledged to count as good for `min-replicas-to-write` (Redis `min-replicas-max-lag`). 0 turns `min-replicas-to-write` off.
min-replicas-to-write: Refuse writes while fewer than this many replicas are good: online, and heard from within `min-replicas-max-lag` seconds (Redis `min-replicas-to-write`). 0 is off. A master cut off from its replicas then refuses writes with NOREPLICAS instead of accepting ones that are lost when the partition heals.
notify-keyspace-events: Keyspace notification events to publish (empty = disabled).
preload-file: Load this file at startup instead of the usual `dump.kdb` and `appendonly.aof`: `aof:<manifest>` restores a sealed backup, `rdb:<file>` a single snapshot (Redis 8.10 `preload-file`). Startup-only; startup fails if the target cannot be loaded.
protected-mode: While the default user has no password, accept clients from this machine only (Redis `protected-mode`). See `src/protected_mode.rs`.
repl-backlog-size: Bytes of the write stream a master keeps for replicas that reconnect (Redis `repl-backlog-size`). A replica that was away for less than this much writing is brought up to date without a full resync.
repl-backlog-ttl: Seconds a master with no replicas keeps that backlog before releasing it (Redis `repl-backlog-ttl`). 0 = never release it.
repl-diskless-load: How a replica loads a full resync (Redis `repl-diskless-load`): disabled | flushdb | on-empty-db — drop the local dataset first, then load: memory for one dataset swapdb — keep serving the local dataset until the new one is loaded, then swap: memory for two
repl-ping-replica-period: Seconds between the PINGs a master writes into the replication stream (Redis `repl-ping-replica-period`). They give an idle link traffic, so a replica can tell "nothing to replicate" apart from "master is gone".
repl-replica-max-backlog-bytes: Max bytes a master will queue for a single replica that isn't keeping up (analogous to Redis's `client-output-buffer-limit slave <hard-limit>`). Once exceeded the replica is disconnected — it must full-resync to catch back up — rather than letting the queue grow without bound.
repl-timeout: Seconds without a byte from the master before a replica declares the link dead and reconnects (Redis `repl-timeout`). Also bounds each step of the handshake. This is what notices a master that was powered off or partitioned away: such a peer never refuses or resets the connection, so without a deadline the replica waits on the kernel's own TCP retransmission limit (~15 minutes) while reporting a healthy link.
replica-full-sync-guard: What a replica does when a full resync would replace its dataset with a smaller one: off    — always accept (Redis behaviour) empty  — refuse a master that has no keys while we hold some shrink — additionally refuse a master holding fewer than `replica-full-sync-guard-ratio` percent of our key count A refused sync keeps the local dataset, leaves the link down, and is retried; the operator overrides with `CONFIG SET replica-full-sync-guard off`.
replicaof: Replicate from master: "host port" (e.g. "127.0.0.1 6379") Pass as two args: --replicaof 127.0.0.1 6379
requirepass: Password required for AUTH (empty = no authentication required)
slowlog-entry-max-string-len: Bytes kept per argument in a slowlog entry (Redis 8.8 `slowlog-entry-max-string-len`).
slowlog-log-slower-than: Slowlog threshold in microseconds (0 = log everything)
slowlog-max-len: Maximum number of slowlog entries to keep
stream-idmp-duration: Default seconds an `XADD ... IDMP` producer/id pair is remembered (Redis 8.6 `stream-idmp-duration`).
stream-idmp-maxsize: Default idempotency ids remembered per producer (Redis 8.6 `stream-idmp-maxsize`).
tls-cluster: The cluster bus over TLS, and the TLS port announced as this node's port, so that what nodes open to each other is TLS (Redis `tls-cluster`). Needs `tls-port`, the certificate, key and CA files.
tls-replication: A replica connects to its master over TLS (Redis `tls-replication`). Implied by `tls-cluster` in a cluster.
